Yes, NVIDIA's gross margin has recovered from its 2025 dip. Here's what the data shows:

## Gross Margin Recovery

The gross margin bottomed at **60.5%** in the quarter ending April 27, 2025 [0001045810-25-000116], then recovered to:
- 72.4% in the quarter ending July 27, 2025 [0001045810-25-000209]
- 73.0% in the quarter ending January 26, 2025 [0001045810-25-000023]
- 73.4% in the quarter ending October 26, 2025 [0001045810-25-000230]
- 74.9% in the quarter ending April 26, 2026 [0001045810-26-000052]
- 75.0% in the quarter ending July 26, 2026 [0001045810-26-000075]

The most recent gross margin of 75.0% has fully recovered to levels comparable to pre-dip periods (78.4% in April 2024, 75.1% in July 2024) [0001045810-24-000124, 0001045810-24-000264].

## Management's Explanation for the Decline

Management attributed the gross margin decline to two primary factors:

1. **$4.5 billion H20 charge**: "Gross margins decreased to 60.5% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 compared to 78.4% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2025, primarily due to a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations and the initial ramp of more sophisticated systems within Data Center." [0001045810-25-000116 | part_i_item_2]

2. **Business model transition**: "Gross margins decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026." [0001045810-26-000021 | part_ii_item_7]

Management also noted that the recovery was aided by improved product mix: "Gross margin increased to 75.0% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 72.4% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026...due to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra." [0001045810-26-000075 | part_i_item_2]
